discovery.city: West Sacramento, California (Sacramento metro; across the Sacramento River from downtown Sacramento)
discovery.team: Athletics (official name is just "Athletics" / "the A's" — MLB and the club dropped any city prefix beginning with the 2025 season; some third-party sites informally write "Sacramento Athletics," which is NOT the official name)
discovery.venue_notes: The Athletics left the Oakland Coliseum after the 2024 season (55 seasons there) and moved to Sutter Health Park, the Triple-A Sacramento River Cats' ballpark in West Sacramento, as a temporary home while a new ballpark is built in Las Vegas. The announced arrangement covers 2025 through 2027, with a club option for a fourth year (2028) if the Las Vegas ballpark is not ready; the team is currently scheduled to open the Las Vegas stadium in 2028. 2026 is their second season in West Sacramento. They share the park with the River Cats, alternating homestands. At ~14,014 capacity it is the smallest ballpark in MLB. Ahead of 2026 the club added private pitcher rooms inside both dugouts ("The Severino Room"), replaced the sod, and made batting-cage and cosmetic upgrades; the 2026 schedule also includes a small set of Athletics home games (reported as six) staged at Las Vegas Ballpark in Summerlin South, NV — CONFIRM before treating Sutter Health Park as the venue for a specific 2026 date. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Athletics_season , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutter_Health_Park , https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-sutter-health-park-in-west-sacramento-to-host-a-s-for-2025-2027-seasons.html , https://www.mlb.com/news/sutter-health-park-undergoing-changes-for-2026

discovery.capacity: 14,014 (10,624 fixed/permanent seats plus outfield grass berms and standing room). Originally 14,611 when it opened as Raley Field in 2000, reduced to 14,414 in 2005 (party deck) and again in 2010 (Diamond Club behind home plate). It is the smallest ballpark in MLB during the Athletics' tenancy.
discovery.capacity_expanded_for_mlb: PARTIALLY — the 2025 renovation for MLB was mostly qualitative (natural grass replacing turf, new two-story clubhouse behind the left-field wall, 75' x 32' videoboard, Wi-Fi 7, new/renovated premium clubs, enlarged dugouts and bullpens to MLB standards) rather than a large seat-count expansion. Sources describe the MLB-use figure as ~14,014 including berm/standing room. CONFIRMED: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutter_Health_Park , https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/sutter-health-park/ , https://www.mlb.com/news/athletics-announce-sutter-health-park-upgrades

orientation.batter_faces: Northeast / east-northeast. Home plate is at the southwest end; the batter looks out toward center field to the NE, with the downtown Sacramento skyline and Tower Bridge beyond right field. Practical consequence: the sun rises behind right field, passes over home plate near midday, and sets beyond the left-field / third-base side, so first-base-side and right-field seats look into the setting sun.
orientation.confidence: CONFIRMED (two independent sources agree on NE/ENE)
orientation.source: https://www.shadedseats.com/sutter-health-park-shaded-seats/ ("Sutter Health Park is oriented to the northeast"; sun "sets behind left field") and https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/sutter-health-park-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more ("east-northeast positioning means the sun reliably goes down in the distance between third base and home plate")

numbering_direction.summary: Lower-bowl (100 level) section numbers INCREASE from the right-field / first-base side, through home plate, toward the third-base side and left field. 101 is the far right-field-line corner; the 105-108 range is the first-base line; 109-113 sit behind home plate; 114-122 run down the third-base line; 123-125 are the left-field corner. Equivalently: numbers DECREASE toward first base/right field and INCREASE toward third base/left field. The 200 (Suite/Club) level follows the same low-number-equals-right-field convention — 201-206 (Sky River Casino Solon Club) sit on the first-base / right-field side.

accessibility.summary: CONFIRMED from the official Athletics access guide. Accessible (wheelchair) and companion seating is offered in ALL price ranges throughout the ballpark. Wheelchair-accessible rows sit at the TOP of most sections and are labeled 'WC' on ticketing/seat-view charts (e.g., sections 105, 111 and 121 all list 'WC' as their last row). Elevator service connects all three levels — Diamond View Dugout, Main Concourse and Suite Level — via the elevator in the Suite Entrance behind Section 113; guests with disabilities get elevator priority. Ballpark-issued wheelchairs can be borrowed and guests can request an escort to and from their seats; wheelchair storage is at the Home Plate Gate, the Right Field Gate and the Guest Services Station. Designated disability drop-off areas are provided outside the park. Groups of 10+ that include disabled guests should email tickets@sutterhealthpark.com and every effort is made to seat the whole party adjacent to the accessible locations.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: MIXED — rows are mostly NUMBERS, but several lower-bowl sections have LETTERED front rows ahead of the numbered rows. Confirmed per-section evidence: Section 102 lists first row 'AA', then 'BB', 'CC', then numbered rows 11, 13, 23, up to 24; Section 121 runs from first row 'AA' through numbered rows 14 and 23 to last row 'WC'; Section 105 has numbered rows from 4 up to last row 'WC'; Section 111 lists first row '1' and numbered rows 1, 5, 11, 14, 23, 25 with last row 'WC'. So: doubled-letter rows (AA, BB, CC) = the closest-to-field rows where they exist; ordinary numbered rows 1-25ish make up the bulk of each section; 'WC' denotes the wheelchair/companion row at the TOP (back) of most sections. Sources: https://aviewfrommyseat.com/venue/Sutter+Health+Park/102/ , /105/ , /111/ , /121/ ; https://www.tickpick.com/blog/athletics-seating-chart-with-seat-views/ ("accessible rows are located at the top of most sections throughout the venue").
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: UNCERTAIN — no venue-specific published rule for Sutter Health Park was found. The only verbatim statements available are generic-to-all-venues boilerplate on ticket resellers' Sutter Health Park pages: TickPick states "seat number 1 is closer to the preceding section" and that "the highest seat number in section" is adjacent to the next section (https://www.tickpick.com/venues/sutter-health-park/seating-chart/ ; identical wording at https://www.simpleseats.com/sutter-health-park-seating-chart/). Applying that rule to this park's confirmed numbering direction (sections increase from right field toward left field) implies seat 1 sits on the LOWER-SECTION-NUMBER edge of each section, i.e. the edge nearer first base / right field, with seat numbers increasing toward third base / left field. TickPick's Athletics guide is consistent with that reading: on the left-field line lower seat numbers are the better (closer to the plate) seats, and on the right-field line higher seat numbers are better (https://www.tickpick.com/blog/athletics-seating-chart-with-seat-views/). TREAT AS INFERRED, NOT CONFIRMED — verify against a live ticket map before relying on it.
discovery.known_obstructions: No published catalogue of obstructed-view seats at Sutter Health Park was found (UNCERTAIN). Practical quirks that are documented: (1) HEAT AND SUN are the dominant issue — Sacramento summer afternoons routinely exceed 100F, the park is the only open-air MLB venue with no structural weather protection to speak of, and most A's games are deliberately scheduled at night for that reason. (2) With the NE orientation, the FIRST-BASE side (101-107) and the 200-level Solon Club sections (201-206) sit in the path of the setting sun and stay sunny the longest; the right-field Home Run Hill berm and the bullpen area get sun the longest of all and have essentially no shade. (3) Behind-the-plate sections 109-113 and the whole THIRD-BASE side (114-122, plus 123-125) fall into shade first — 109-113 pick up consistent shade from the upper-deck overhang around 2-3pm, and the entire third-base side is shaded by late afternoon. For early-afternoon starts (12:05-1:05pm) almost nothing is shaded except the back rows of 103-105 under the overhang. (4) One dissenting source (theshadium.com) describes the third-base side as the SUNNIER side and the first-base side as the better open option — this contradicts the other two shade sources and the confirmed NE orientation, so treat the shadium reading as an outlier. (5) The lower bowl is a single deck foul pole to foul pole, so overhang-related sightline blockage is limited to the back rows under the second deck. Sources: https://www.shadedseats.com/sutter-health-park-shaded-seats/ ; https://gamedayguides.com/sutter-health-park-as-guide/ ; https://theshadium.com/blog/shaded-seats-sutter-health-park ; https://grokipedia.com/page/Sutter_Health_Park ; https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/sutter-health-park/

No 200-level section was confirmed as directly behind home plate; suites and the press box occupy that arc but numbered 201-206 are on the first-base/right-field side and section 201 is tagged 'outfield'.
Exact section-to-section boundaries of the Dugout Club (108-116 per TickPick) vs the Governor's Club (unspecified 'infield') vs Homeplate Club A-D are not published by the club.
Concert / non-baseball configurations and any concert-only sections are undocumented.
No verbatim, venue-specific seat-1 orientation statement exists on any section page; the seat-1 side is inferred from generic reseller boilerplate plus the confirmed section-numbering direction.

Whether the left-field berm is sold as ticketed 'Lawn' GA for Athletics games (as opposed to River Cats games) — MLB's own guide names only the right-field Toyota Home Run Hill as the GA berm, while Wikipedia and In The Ballparks describe berms in both outfield corners.
